d: A hypothalamic neuropeptide that stimulates GnRH neurons through its receptor and helps restart pulsatile GnRH at puberty; gain-of-function mutations cause central precocious puberty and loss-of-function mutations block puberty.
Maturation of the adrenal zona reticularis in mid-childhood, which raises DHEA and DHEA-S under ACTH and causes pubic and axillary hair, body odor and acne independent of the gonadal axis.
The skeletal maturity read from an X-ray of the left hand and wrist; sex steroids advance it, so it runs ahead in precocious puberty and behind in constitutional delay and hypogonadism.
A benign congenital mass of hypothalamic tissue that can contain its own GnRH neurons; it is the classic brain lesion behind central precocious puberty in young boys and can cause laughing seizures.

A postzygotic activating GNAS mutation that keeps Gs signaling on in scattered cells, causing peripheral precocious puberty from autonomous ovarian cysts, café-au-lait macules and polyostotic fibrous dysplasia.

t: Constitutional delay of growth and puberty
d: The most common cause of late puberty: a healthy, short child with a delayed bone age and often a late-maturing parent, whose puberty eventually starts on its own.

Familial male-limited precocious puberty from an activating mutation of the LH receptor: Leydig cells secrete testosterone without LH, so a young boy virilizes with a low LH, modestly enlarged testes and an advanced bone age.
